subject: Home Economics
examFormat: The aim of the UTME Home Economics syllabus is to prepare candidates for the Board's examination. The course objectives are to: acquire knowledge on the concepts and principles of Home Economics education; apply the principles of Foods and Nutrition to planning, selection and preparation of meals and the adoption of food hygiene and safety; equip students with knowledge and skills in Clothing and Textiles; and apply the principles of Home Management in home and family living. The syllabus is arranged in four sections: Home Economics Education, Home Management, Foods and Nutrition, and Clothing and Textile.
excluded: Two objective lines in the source ('determine the effect of exercise and cosmetics on the skin' and 'describe the structure of the sensory organs / suggest ways of taking care of the sensory organs') appear at a page break after Kitchen Safety and Hygiene but do not belong to any topic listed in the syllabus text (extraction artefact); they were left out. The internet and exam-aid titles in the reading list were kept as given.

Home Economics for Schools and College — Okeke, S.U.N. (Africana First Publishers, 2009)

topics.name: Home Economics
objectives: examine the importance of Home Economics to the individual, family, society and nation
identify the objectives of Home Economics
determine the scope of Home Economics
topics.content: Meaning, scope and importance of Home Economics. Objectives and ideals of Home Economics.

topics.name: Areas and Careers in Home Economics
objectives: recommend possible vocations in the different areas of Home Economics
relate Home Economics to each vocation
assess the benefits of each vocation to the individual, society and nation
identify current vocations in Home Economics
identify sources of career information
topics.content: Home management (interior decoration, credit management, florist). Foods and nutrition (catering, dietetics, nutritionist, public health education, etc.). Clothing and textile (textile designing). Family and child development (early and childhood education). Teaching. Counselling. Media. Research.

topics.name: Interrelationship of Home Economics with Other Subjects
objectives: compare the different areas of study which have relationship with Home Economics
determine the contributions of these subjects to Home Economics
topics.content: Biology, Geography, Chemistry, Physics, Agricultural Science, Fine Arts, Economics, Mathematics etc.

topics.name: Principles of Home Management
objectives: state the meaning of Home Management
identify steps involved in the management process
determine issues for decision-making in the home
describe the role of motivators in Home Management
topics.content: Meaning of home management. Steps in the management process. Decision-making: meaning and process. Motivation for home management e.g. goals, values, standards, needs and wants, likes and dislikes.

topics.name: Resources
objectives: identify the resources available to the individual and family
describe the pattern of work plan
apply the principle of time management to work simplification in the home
identify the sources of income available to an individual and family
determine the means of family saving
give reasons for saving family income
determine the steps involved in family budgeting
suggest alternative resources for Home Management
analyse the principles of money management
state other material resources available to individual and family
topics.content: Human resources: definition and types. Time management: definition and pattern, types of work time, factors influencing the use of time, advantages of time management. Energy: definition and reasons for energy management; work simplification - its purpose and application; guidelines for work simplification and time saving gadgets. Skills, creativity, attitudes etc. Material resources: definition and types. Income and money management: meaning and types of income, principles of money management, household budgeting (steps in making a budget), economic security of the family, bank accounts, traditional savings, building societies and insurance.

topics.name: Family Living
objectives: compare types of family
identify roles of family members
differentiate between the types of relationships that exist in the family
determine the factors that influence family relationships
describe factors that influence family relationships
identify characteristics and problems of adolescents
compare the basic personality profiles (extrovert, introvert)
identify types of family crises and ways of solving them
identify sources of conflict and solution strategies
identify types of human rights and human rights violation
suggest remedies for breach of human rights
identify factors that hinder communication in the family
determine factors that enhance communication in the family
identify the advantages and disadvantages of ICT
topics.content: Definition and types of family; advantages and disadvantages of family types; the family life cycle. Family relationships: husband/wife, parent/child and brother/sister (sibling) relationships; factors that influence family relationships. Basic personality profiles: meaning of personality; extroversion, introversion and anxiety/stability. Adolescents and their problems. Family crises. Conflict and conflict resolution. Human rights: meaning of human rights and fundamental human rights, rights of women and children, violation of human rights. Communication and the role of ICT in the family.

topics.name: Marriage and Reproductive Health
objectives: differentiate between types of marriages in Nigeria
compare the advantages and disadvantages of inter-tribal marriages
analyse the role of courtship and engagement in marriages
identify the different ways of planning a family
state types, causes and prevention of sexually transmitted infections and diseases
topics.content: Meanings of marriage and sex education. Boy/girl relationship: courtship; factors to consider when choosing a partner. Preparation for marriage: meaning and purpose of engagement; types of marriage (Islamic, Christian, Court and Traditional); planning a family. Reproductive health: sexually transmitted infections/diseases (STIs/STDs and HIV/AIDS) etc.

topics.name: Pregnancy and Childbirth
objectives: describe the process of reproduction from conception to birth
describe the care an infant needs from birth to 5 years
determine the factors that affect pregnancy
differentiate between the stages of labour
identify the symptoms of common ailments in children
mention types of play materials
trace the stages of development in children
recommend suitable play materials for children
identify responsibilities of parents
topics.content: Menstruation, pregnancy and childbirth, labour, delivery and post-natal care. Childcare: baby's layette, care of the baby, toilet training, bathing, feeding, weaning, etc. Care of toddlers: common ailments in children; immunization. Child development: good habits and character training; play and play materials. Parenting: meaning and importance; responsibilities of parents.

topics.name: Housing the Family
objectives: differentiate between a house and a home
identify the factors that influence residential choice
describe items that beautify living areas
suggest suitable colours, textures and other related factors that should be considered in interior decoration
determine factors that influence choice and arrangement of furniture
compare different floral arrangements
identify types of ornament and fixtures
describe the care of ornaments and fixtures
identify utilities in the home
appraise the advantages and disadvantages of these utilities in relation to their alternatives
topics.content: Houses and home: types of houses, factors that affect the choice of a house, ways of acquiring a house. Interior decoration: wall finishing and the application of principles of art and design to colours, textures, lines and proportions; flower arrangements. Furniture and furnishings in the home: types; factors that affect choices and position. Utilities in the home: water (source, uses, purification, etc.); household fuels e.g. gas, coal, electricity, kerosene, firewood and sawdust; electricity (related terms, generation, safety, etc.); communication devices e.g. GSM, computer etc.

topics.name: Home Surfaces
objectives: identify common surfaces in the homes
mention cleaning agents and their uses in the home
identify materials needed for preparing local cleaning agents
compare the care of wood, plastic, concrete, rugs, mats, linoleum etc
topics.content: Types and care of surfaces and coverings e.g. wood, tiles, Formica, concretes, plastics, linoleums, mats, rugs and terrazzo. Identification, preparation and use of cleaning agents such as water, soap, abrasives, polish, etc. Care of home surfaces and coverings e.g. washing, sweeping, dusting, shampooing, buffing, polishing.

topics.name: Sanitation in the Home
objectives: identify types of waste water
suggest ways of disposing household refuse
identify common household pests and their control
identify some diseases transmitted by pests
describe sources of pollution
mention the health hazards of pollution
topics.content: Drainage systems: types and care. Disposal of household refuse. Household pests and control. Pollution and health hazards.

topics.name: Consumer Education
objectives: explain the importance of consumer education
identify the different types of markets
describe the various consumer agents
identify sources of consumer advice and information
apply the principles of consumer education to wise shopping
identify the types of media used by advertisers
describe their advantages and disadvantages
explain the rights and responsibilities of the consumer
identify the functions of government agencies and regulatory bodies
topics.content: Meaning and importance of consumer education. Definition and types of market. Distributors or consumer agents. Sources of consumer information. Purchasing practices. Advertising. Consumer rights and responsibilities. Government agencies and regulatory bodies.

topics.name: Foods and Nutrition
objectives: describe the following: food nutrients, carbohydrates, minerals, fat and oil, vitamin, protein and water
identify the different classes of food
describe the effect of nutrition on health status
identify factors affecting good nutrition
describe the process which breaks down large food molecules
recommend the nutritional needs for special groups

determine the reasons for the nutritional needs of expectant/lactating mothers, infants and toddlers; sedentary/manual workers; children between 5 and 8 years; adolescents, the aged, invalids and convalescents
topics.content: Definition of foods and nutrition. Classification of nutrients, their sources and functions, deficiency diseases. Classification of foods: cereals, fats and oils, milk and milk products, meat, fish, pulses, nuts, fruits, vegetables, etc. Nutrition and health: relationship of nutrition and health; factors affecting nutrition e.g. income, food in season, availability of food, etc. The digestive system. Nutrition for special groups e.g. infants, toddlers, adolescents, manual workers, etc.

topics.name: Meal Planning
objectives: identify factors that influence the choice and preparation of food for the family
plan meals for special occasions e.g. weddings, birthdays, anniversaries, etc
plan meals for special groups e.g. vegetarians, invalids, convalescents, HIV/AIDS patients, COVID patients, etc
identify types of snacks/beverages and their functions
compare types of table setting
describe table manners and qualities of a good host
topics.content: Principles of meal planning. Dietary needs and meals for special occasions and groups. Preparation and serving of meals. Snacks and beverages: meaning, types and functions. Table setting, table manners and hostessing.

topics.name: Cookers and Cooking
objectives: identify types of cookers, their choice and care
enumerate reasons for cooking
group the methods of cooking into moist methods, dry methods, fast methods and slow methods
determine the method of heat transfer in the various methods of cooking
topics.content: Types, choice and care of cookers e.g. gas, electric, microwave, etc. Reasons for cooking. Cooking terms. Methods of cooking e.g. boiling, stewing, baking, steaming, etc.; moist and dry methods of cooking. Methods of heat transfer e.g. conduction, convection and radiation.

topics.name: Flours and Uses
objectives: identify types of flours and their uses
select appropriate raising agents for basic mixtures
use flour to produce assorted food items
topics.content: Types and uses of flours. Raising agents e.g. air, yeast, palm wine, steam, etc.

topics.name: Basic Mixtures
objectives: differentiate between batters and pastries
use batters and pastries for different purposes
topics.content: Pastries and batters: definition and uses.

topics.name: Scientific Methods in Foods and Nutrition
objectives: demonstrate skills in unit measurements
detect the nutrients in a given food
develop basic recipes in food preparation
topics.content: Measure units and accuracy. Various nutrient tests in food e.g. tests for protein, fats and carbohydrates. Recipe development.

topics.name: The Kitchen
objectives: describe types and arrangement of kitchen
compare large and small kitchen equipment and tools
specify factors to consider in selecting kitchen tools and equipment
topics.content: Types of kitchen. Arrangement. Tools and equipment: selection, use and care.

topics.name: Kitchen Safety and Hygiene
objectives: identify common accidents in the kitchen, their causes and preventive measures
suggest ways of making the kitchen a safe place
specify items which should be included in a first aid kit
suggest simple first aid for scalds, cuts, bleeding, burns, etc
identify ways in which food is contaminated
compare communicable and non-communicable diseases and their preventive measures
topics.content: Common accidents in the kitchen: causes of accidents and preventive measures. First aid: definition; components of a first aid kit; simple first aid for burns, scalds, cuts, bruises, bleeding, electric shock, poisoning, choking and bites. Kitchen, personal and food hygiene; communicable and non-communicable diseases.

topics.name: Food Storage and Preservation
objectives: identify agents of food spoilage
describe the principles involved in the preservation and storage of foods
compare the advantages and disadvantages of food preservation methods
identify convenience foods
compare the advantages and disadvantages of using convenience foods
identify guidelines for selecting convenience foods
identify additives used in foods
compare the advantages and disadvantages of rechauffe dishes
topics.content: Meaning and purpose of preservation: causes of food spoilage, principles of food preservation, methods of food preservation. Convenience foods: definition and types, guidelines for selection, use of convenience foods. Food additives: types and uses. Rechauffe dishes: meaning, rules and types; advantages and disadvantages of rechauffe.

topics.name: Home Gardening
objectives: identify gardening tools
explain the importance of home gardening
describe the procedures involved in home gardening
topics.content: Definition. Common gardening tools. Advantages of home gardening. Types of soil. Plants and crops suitable for home garden. Preparation and care of home garden.

topics.name: Fibres and Fabrics
objectives: identify the characteristics of fibre
differentiate between methods of fabric construction using diagrams
state reasons for giving finishes to fabrics
state the uses and importance of locally made fabric
compare types of labels found on clothing
state the importance of labels on garments
topics.content: Origin of fibres: definition of textile terms e.g. fibres, fabrics, yarn, staple, filament, blends, etc. Locally made fabrics e.g. aso-oke, Okene cloth, Benue cloth, Akwete, Gwado, etc. Classification and properties of fibres e.g. cotton, rayon, silk, etc. Fabric finishes: moth-proofing, embossing, durable pleating, flame-proofing, stain-repellent, print e.g. tie and dye, screen printing etc. Textile care labels: meaning and types; recognition of washing, cleaning and ironing symbols, wool symbols, etc.

topics.name: Sewing Equipment and Garment Construction
objectives: identify the types, parts and faults of a sewing machine
identify basic tools and equipment used in garment construction
describe various processes in garment construction
apply basic processes in garment construction
identify style features to enhance the beauty and quality of garments
apply decorative designs on fabrics
apply the knowledge of sewing to mend and renovate garments
compare the process of making batik/tie and dye, screen printing and resist dyeing
relate body figures to the selection of styles and fabrics
determine factors which affect the choice of clothing
identify factors to consider in wardrobe planning
describe the terms good grooming, dress sense, accessories and colour harmony
topics.content: Sewing machine, basic tools and equipment: types, use and care. Basic processes in garment construction: basic stitches, seams, edge finishes, crossway strips, etc. Style features: collars, yokes, pockets, frills, cuts, belts, etc. Arrangement of fullness: darts, tucks, gathering, pleats, smocking, shirring, etc. Decorative design: embroidery, needlecraft, tatting, crocheting, knitting, appliqué, patchwork and soft furnishing. Simple processes and mending garments: patching, darning, renovation, batik/tie and dye. Garment construction: figure types, basic body measurement and pattern drafting; choice of styles for different figures; factors influencing the choice of fabric. Wardrobe planning and maintenance: basic rules in wardrobe planning; factors affecting wardrobe planning (weather, occupation, personal features etc.). Good grooming, dress sense and accessories: definition; types and choice of accessories.

topics.name: Laundry and Care of Clothes
objectives: arrange in correct order the processes involved in washing and finishing of clothing
describe the role of laundry agents
suggest ways of removing common stains
describe laundry agents, stains and ironing temperatures
topics.content: Washing and finishing process: sorting, mending, removal of stains, soaking, washing, rinsing, drying, ironing and airing. Laundry agents: water, detergents, soaps, stiffeners, disinfectants etc. Stains: meaning, types, agents; process of removal. Iron and ironing temperatures.
